scope: Independent adversarial review of evaluation/pre-exposure/filter.mjs; no production or controller changes.

findings.mechanism: Binary assignment expressions are not rejected. The traversal allows a dynamic SQL concatenation in a function parameter default, while the mask range begins at the function declaration and hides that parameter source.
findings.reproduction: review-tests.mjs: default-parameter assignment with dynamic SQL is masked
findings.impact: An actionable dynamic SQL construction in a default argument disappears from pre-exposure source output under a whole-function ordinary mask.
findings.requiredDisposition: Do not enable this masking gate until all effectful and SQL-construction expressions in parameters, decorators, and function body are rejected or the emitted mask excludes unverified signature and body fragments.

findings.location: filterRows statement and visit checks; auditSource driver candidate classification
findings.mechanism: A direct driver call is ordinary when its first argument has Serene provenance. The filter neither verifies additional driver arguments nor rejects assignment expressions nested in them.
findings.reproduction: review-tests.mjs: driver-argument assignment is masked despite unverified binding use
findings.impact: Unreviewed binding substitution and an unrelated dynamic SQL assignment disappear with an otherwise ordinary function.
findings.requiredDisposition: Require an exact recognized execution-call shape, including all relevant arguments, and reject assignments/update expressions before masking.

findings.mechanism: A property named query on any parameter receiver is a syntactic ordinary driver candidate. No native-driver identity is established.
findings.reproduction: review-tests.mjs: syntactic query receiver identity is not established before masking
findings.impact: The filter can hide a function whose receiver is an unknown wrapper. This matches the audit's documented candidate-identity limit, so it must not be represented as positive native-driver verification.
findings.requiredDisposition: Either retain such receivers or state and enforce that masking only attests Serene text construction, never execution identity or driver binding correctness.

nonfindings: Existing suite covers parse failure, computed calls, unknown helper calls, unsupported sinks, same-function dynamic SQL, stale source, and same-line adjacent ranges.
Line fragments that do not byte-match the current source are retained by filterRows, which is conservative for source-coordinate mismatch.

PREX-001.change: filterRows rejects every parameter initializer and every non-identifier parameter binding before it considers a complete-function mask; assignment and update expressions also invalidate a candidate anywhere in the declaration traversal.
PREX-001.regression: review-tests.mjs: REGRESSION: default-parameter assignment with dynamic SQL prevents masking

PREX-002.change: filterRows accepts a driver call only when its first argument is a direct identifier .text property. Later arguments may be primitive literals or identifiers, or direct .values/.params properties on that same bound identifier. Assignment and arbitrary expression arguments invalidate masking.
regressions: review-tests.mjs: REGRESSION: driver-argument assignment with dynamic SQL prevents masking
review-tests.mjs: REGRESSION: arbitrary values property in a driver argument prevents masking

PREX-003.change: No receiver-identity claim was added. Ordinary masking remains an attestation of source construction plus syntactic candidate shape, not proof that the receiver is a native driver or that bindings are semantically correct.
